rows.label: gemma3-12b-4bit
rows.qualitative: Structurally the candidate is compliant — five labeled sections in order, each D item tagged with an origin, no stray commentary — but substantively it captures only the last two turns of a nine-turn session and almost nothing verifiable. Entire workstreams vanish: the ~/.claude-home zsh wrapper that actually resolved task 2, the whole TypeSafe skill summary, the jev-distill-routing repo, and every number the session produced (v1.1.17, 65 SPINE entries, 22,585 rubric chars, $0.50 cap blowout, $1.72 spend, 2.7s median choose, 4/4 hit rate, 41% never distilled, $0.002/session). Worse, it asserts the routing baseline as a future step when it had already run, and it invents rationales for two D-section decisions (the exchanges unit and the separate repo) while crediting the assistant's arithmetic to the user. Its genuine strengths are narrow: the cold-read pivot, the exchanges concept, Jev pricing, ground-truth need, and the recall-over-precision policy are all correctly reported — but section A is largely a vague paraphrase of failures whose diagnostic detail is the reference's main value, and section C is generic praise that would fit almost any session.

rows.label: gptoss-20b-mxfp4
rows.qualitative: The candidate gets the headline shape right — the by-design home-trust finding and zsh wrapper, the $0.50 budget-cap failure and $1.00 re-run, the ~2.7s/~13s/$0.38 baseline numbers, the pivot to Jev turn-filtering, and the Jev cost arithmetic ($0.042/Mtok → ~$0.002/session) — and it observes the five-section structure with origin labels in D. It is far weaker than the reference on process detail and provenance: essentially all of the debugging texture (ugrep complexity error, illegal byte sequence, ToolSearch→curl fallback, script iterations), the knowledge-base grounding (working-conventions.md, headless-clean-agents.md, the 2026-08-02 "marks" case), the concrete design decisions (linux-ssh topic and #48/65 rationale, real config dir due to Keychain OAuth, ≤400-char rubric / 22.6k chars, arm-B bar, cold-read retargeting), and the entire aura-distill status answer (v1.1.17, 114 files, 99k words, SPINE 79/80) are absent. Its most serious defect is systematic misattribution: sections B, C and D repeatedly credit the user with facts, explanations and directives that were the assistant's own (TypeSafe/SPINE details, repo layout, topic choice, "update README", the separate-repo preference), and it invents user emotions and a "several hours" duration. Net: a thin but mostly readable skeleton with low recall and several confidently wrong actor/origin assignments.

rows.label: haiku-1
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strongest in section E and in the pivot design (exchanges, session-level pass, $0.002/session, cold-read target), where it matches the reference closely and stays grounded. It is much weaker in section A, omitting nearly all tool-level friction the reference captures (zsh `======`, transcript-parser rewrite, spine_entries patch and rubric sizing, Keychain/config-dir deviation, the chosen linux-ssh topic, the arm-B bar), and it never names the repo path. Section C is its biggest liability: several user attributions are invented or reversed (user 'cited' the repos convention, 'did mental math', 'invoked live data is sacred', 'understood TypeSafe immediately', 'accepted via follow-up' when no follow-up exists), and D introduces non-spec origins ('Pragmatism', 'Principle') and a fabricated security rationale. Net: decent structure and outcome fidelity, but recall of granular evidence is low and grounding in the user-model sections is unreliable.

rows.label: opus-2
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strong on the failure ledger (Section A) and decision table (Section D): it reproduces nearly every tool-level failure with exact error strings, IDs, token counts and dollar figures, and its D origins match the reference almost row-for-row, including the 41%/59% split, $0.002/session, and the marks-case reframing. Relative to the reference it is weaker on a handful of specifics — it omits that ~/repos did not exist on the Mac, the <a prior project>/2026-09-09 provenance of the headless recipe, the user's "free arithmetic before designing" rule, the concrete cell-isolation flags (Read/Glob/Grep, --strict-mcp-config, --max-turns 8), and the enumerated 3-step plan — and it undercounts tool calls (~30 vs ≈37). Grounding is high; the only distortions are presenting the ~/repos path as a KB fact (the KB says <user-repos-root>), asserting the headless recipe was "written on Windows" (unstated), and the tool-call count. Section B is slightly diluted by mixing "KB facts surfaced" into a corrections section, but no fabricated claims were found.

rows.label: qwen38-27b-4bit
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strong on the second half of the session — the pivot, the "marks" precedent, the exchange-vs-turn reframing, the cost arithmetic, and nearly every section-D decision from turn 9 are captured with correct numbers and defensible origin labels, and the spec is cleanly satisfied (A–E in order, every D row carries an origin, no stray commentary). It is materially weaker on the mechanical/tooling layer of the early session: the "Enough evidence already" parallelization, the PERMISSION_MODES fragment, the empty ToolSearch/WebFetch fallback to curl, both transcript-parser iterations, the in-place spine_entries() patch with its ≤400-char rubric and 22,585-char budget check, the missing ~/repos directory, the NON-NEGOTIABLE repos convention, the git attribution decision, and the self-caught unverified `answers.file.choice` field name are all absent — roughly a quarter of the reference set. Grounding is mostly solid, but there are five real defects: an invented 119k–339k cache-read range, "4 valid cells" when only 3 were valid, and three over-claims about the user (that he knows what Jev is, that the ledger-as-ground-truth was his, and that he speaks experimental-design vocabulary) — the first of which directly inverts a reference growth edge. Net: a well-organized summary that reads more confidently than its evidence in section C and slightly padded in the numbers, while under-recording the session's tool-level failure texture and its convention/directive provenance.

rows.label: qwen38-27b-8bit-nothink
rows.qualitative: The candidate is structurally clean — all five sections in order, every D item tagged with an origin (often a defensible dual tag), and no stray commentary — and it is strong on the D/E material: the exchange-projection arithmetic, Jev cost, recall tuning, ground-truth ledger, headless-vs-Agent rationale and baseline outcome numbers are all faithfully reproduced. Its main weakness is a narrativized failure arc: it asserts the Python byte-scan succeeded and yielded the decisive trust string, when in fact both Python passes failed and the conclusion rested on the earlier `strings | grep`; it also miscounts the attempts (4 vs 5) and invents two "wrong assumptions" by the assistant (editing ~/.claude.json, and owning the routing target that was actually the user's idea). Recall is thin on knowledge-base provenance — the 2026-08-02 "marks" precedent, the cold-read/never-distilled reframing of the pivot target, the 41% figure, working-conventions.md, the NON-NEGOTIABLE repo convention, the headless-cell recipe deviation and the rubric-sizing decision are all missing — as are several smaller friction beats (ToolSearch/WebFetch fallback, transcript-parser iteration, PERMISSION_MODES fragment) and quantitative metadata (11 transcripts, 2 commits, turn/tool counts). Net: a well-formed, mostly grounded summary that over-smooths the debugging story and under-reports the knowledge-base reasoning that gave the reference its sharpest insights.

rows.label: qwen38-27b-8bit-think
rows.qualitative: The candidate is structurally clean — all five sections in order, every section-D item carrying an explicit origin label (often with a secondary origin), no stray commentary — and its coverage of the narrative arc (bug-vs-by-design correction, "your call" delegation, gated execution, the post-baseline pivot, exchanges vs turns, cold-read targeting, ground truth from the ledger) is strong. It is materially weaker on numbers and mid-session engineering detail: it drops the 55,155 cache tokens/$0.576 cold-cell anatomy, the 22,585-char ≤400-char rubric sizing and multi-file-bullet rule, the 41% never-distilled figure, ~$0.002/session, the ~10x projection cut, 11 transcripts, 114 files, 2 commits, the git-identity convention, the <a prior project> provenance of the headless recipe, and — notably — the disclosed ~/.claude-home `-r`/`--continue` trade-off and the transcript-parser iteration. Its grounding is mostly solid, but it invents two assistant errors that never happened (an assumption that config editing would fix home trust; a pre-baseline hypothesis that routing was the expensive step) and inverts two user-behavior readings, recasting the "is it installed / what does it do" questions and the "bug" framing as demonstrated expertise where the reference treats them as growth edges. Net: better than the reference on origin labelling discipline and failure-by-failure command detail, weaker on quantitative fidelity and honest characterization of user knowledge gaps.

rows.label: qwen38-9b-4bit
rows.qualitative: The candidate is well-formed structurally — all five sections in order, every D row tagged with an origin, no stray commentary — and it captures the session's spine (budget-cap failure and the $1 rerun, the by-design trust finding, the linux-ssh topic rationale, the cold-read reframe, the $1.72 / 2.7s numbers, the one-call session-level pass). But its recall is shallow: roughly two-thirds of the reference claims are absent or only partial, including the entire answer to the user's first question (v1.1.17, 114 files, ~99k words, SPINE at 79/80), the no-API-key state, the Keychain/config-dir constraint, the -r/--continue trade-off, the repo/commit conventions, the arm-B bar, the recall-tuning policy, the ledger ground truth, and every open decision awaiting the user. It also contains one outright fabrication — that the `answers.file.choice` field name was "verified on first call" and confirmed correct, when no Jev call was ever made — plus several actor inversions (the user, not the assistant, proposed per-turn filtering and raised the chunking worry) and an invented "impatience" read of a go-ahead the assistant itself solicited. Compared with the reference, section C is the weakest: it converts strengths into growth edges, misses all three real growth edges, and stretches "live data is sacred" into a benchmarking preference it elevates to the session's key insight.

rows.label: sonnet-1
rows.qualitative: The candidate is strong on sections B–E: it captures the pivot, the marks-case redirect, the exchanges/session-pass design, the ground-truth plan, and the open asks with correct origins, and its D section is well-labelled. It is materially weaker on section A grounding: it inverts the outcome of the binary search (crediting Python re.finditer with the confirming evidence when the string literals came from the first strings|grep and both Python passes were empty/garbled), fabricates a "user explicitly corrected task 2" framing that it then retracts in the same bullet, over-claims the cold cell cost relative to three warm cells, and wrongly asserts the user has deep familiarity with Jev primitives when the user asked what the skill does. Recall gaps cluster around fine-grained harness details (rubric ≤400 chars / 22.6k chars, spine_entries patch, arm-B bar, answers.file.choice verification, commit attribution, cell isolation flags, zsh ====== glitch, transcript-parser retry) and a few user-model growth edges.
